sources.quote: Since 2013, jail incarceration rates have increased by 26 percent in rural jurisdictions.
sources.searcher_note: Same measure (rural vs urban jail incarceration rate), window 2013-2019; page also says urban rates fell 22 percent since 2013 and rural rates were more than double urban in 2019. No 2023 figure.

sources.quote: And today, people in rural counties are more than twice as likely to go to jail as people in urban areas.
sources.searcher_note: Rewrite of a New York Times piece dated 2019-12-13 (NYT page itself not found); also says urban jail populations fell 18 percent and rural rose 27 percent since 2013.

sources.quote: By spring 2024, incarceration had returned to 2019 levels in many states and in rural counties across the board.
sources.searcher_note: Post-pandemic window: rural jail population up 2.2 percent 2022-2024; no per-100K rural vs urban numbers on the web page.

sources.quote: Rural counties have seen the closest return to 2019 population tallies, while urban county jails have done the best job of maintaining declines.
sources.searcher_note: Same direction for the post-2019 window (rural rebound, urban declines held); population counts, not rates.

sources.quote: Rural areas still have the highest jail incarceration rates by far, with more than half the people incarcerated in local jails being held outside of the nation
sources.searcher_note: Incarceration Trends data release; states rural rates highest, no specific rural/urban rate figures.

sources.quote: While the rate at which legally presumed innocent people are held in jail pretrial has grown 223% nationwide since 1970, it has risen 436% in rural counties
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: Out of Sight report release; rural counties have the highest jail rates and increasingly rent beds to other agencies (the held-for-others driver).

notes: All sources are Vera (the dataset's own publisher) or a rewrite of a 2019 NYT story; the rural jail boom is widely published by Vera itself, as the lead's watch_out says. No source found gives the 2023 per-100K rural (563) vs urban (227) rates or the 2.5x ratio; the closest is 'more than double' for 2019. Nothing found on Butts County GA or Yazoo County MS jail growth or local holds (searches returned roster/aggregator pages only). No disagreeing source found. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found.
